findings.where: Screen 7 'Three devices, one job' and the explain's device paragraph
findings.what: The device comparison gives the IGBT only its strengths ('suits high voltages and currents') and never its cost, the slower turn-off the brief promised and lesson 7's dead time relies on ('One disadvantage of the IGBT over a standard BJT is its slower turn-off time', research notes). It also never says why the BJT's steady base current is a burden (the brief's 5 A of base current for 100 A at a beta of 20), so Dan cannot say why each device gets chosen.

findings.where: Screen 9 'The edges' and the explain's switching paragraph
findings.what: 'Each edge costs a burst of heat, about 1 mJ' is a number with no rule shown on screen. The working (a straight sweep averages a sixth of 600 V x 20 A, which is 2000 W, for 0.5 us, giving 1 mJ) is only in the build notes, so the 20 W on screen 9 and the whole of screen 10 rest on a figure he cannot work out.

findings.where: Every SHOW screen (1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11): the live line under the picture
findings.what: The caption under the picture repeats the sums already in the text above it, so each SHOW screen carries 109 to 122 words. Screen 9 has 90 words of text plus 'Flipping fully on and off at 10 kHz, the switch makes 20 W while on and 20 W in its edges. That is 40 W in all. The junction sits at 60 °C.' That is the 'too much text after the diagrams' Dan flagged: cut the caption to the one number that changes, or trim the text.

The demonstration only opens the switch with no diode, and nothing on screen asks Dan to tick Freewheeling diode. Yet the read sentence describes the step to 601 V and the current dying away round the diode, so the cure, half of the screen's point, appears only if he finds the toggle himself. Add 'Tick the diode and open it again' and have the play run both cases.

Six footnotes ([^5], [^3], [^4], [^6], [^1], [^2]) break the 'at most a few, only on a rule or value he might look up' rule. [^3] and [^4] sit in back-to-back sentences on a small transistor's 600 mW and 24 mW, and [^5] and [^6] sit on plain statements. Keep the switching-loss rule and the 0.7 V, and drop the rest.

findings.where: Screen 1, the 'Heat against the gate setting' plot
findings.what: The plot is already drawn in full, with its 3000 W peak at 50%, before any words mention it. That gives away screen 2's answer (zero at 0%) and the surprise screen 3 is built around. Show the plot from screen 3, where the text introduces it.
The 90-word paragraph and the Transistor picker fill the first phone view, so the circuit and the gate slider, the things to look at and move, start below the fold.

The brief's one-line look-ahead is missing: a transistor held half on on purpose is an amplifier, taught in Instrumentation and control. Without it, 'half on is the worst case' can read as 'half on is always wrong'.

findings.where: Practice bullet 'Fit a freewheeling diode across a DC coil that a transistor switches'
findings.what: The bullet states this as a rule for every case. The brief's nuance is lost: many devices already carry a diode, so an extra one is not always needed.
'A contactor's would not' overstates the case: a contactor's contacts do warm a little and arc on breaking. 'A contactor's make far less' would be true.

'It is fitted to block the supply' and 'the coil sees only its drop' are cryptic on a first read. Say 'It points so the supply cannot push current through it' and 'only the diode's drop, about 0.7 V'.
The right answer 'No, the switch makes about 1080 W' wraps with the 'W' alone on its own line. Join every number to its unit with a non-breaking space in the answer labels.

findings.where: Screen 6 puzzle 'What the sink can shed'
findings.what: The question needs the 0.5 °C per watt from screen 5, but neither the question nor the setting line restates it. Add it to the question.
The edges are drawn about 6 us wide on an axis labelled in real milliseconds, while the text says 0.5 us. Mark them as widened in the key.
The plot's y axis prints '3,000' and '2,000', while every sentence and readout says '3000'. Use one form.

The brief's gate-drive picture (a pulse fills the gate, another empties it) is not drawn. The drive box shows a steady level that rises with the gate setting, so 'draws almost no current except while it changes over' is told, not shown.
